questions.title: How does producer‑consumer warp‑specialization avoid deadlock in FlashAttention‑3?
questions.question_body: In Algorithm 1 the authors split a CTA into producer and consumer warp‑groups and use a circular shared‑memory buffer with stages. I am confused about how the synchronization works: when a producer issues a TMA load for \(K_j,V_j\) it "commits to notify" the consumer, but the consumer may already be waiting for that same stage. How does the implementation guarantee that neither side blocks forever, especially when the number of stages \(s\) is small? Is there a specific ordering of barrier calls or a hardware guarantee that resolves this?

questions.title: What are the exact layout constraints for FP8 WGMMA operands and how are they satisfied?
questions.question_body:
Section 2.3 states that FP8 WGMMA only accepts k‑major operand layout, unlike FP16 which accepts both mn‑major and k‑major. The paper mentions an in‑kernel transpose of \(V\) tiles using LDSM/STSM instructions. Could someone clarify:
1) What memory stride order defines "k‑major" for a tile of shape \(B_c \times d\)?
2) How does the LDSM/STSM sequence accomplish the transpose without extra global memory traffic?
3) How are the register permutations (the \{d0 d1 d4 d5 ...\} pattern) derived from the accumulator layout?

questions.title: Why does overlapping softmax with WGMMA improve utilization despite data dependencies?
questions.question_body: The paper explains that softmax is low‑throughput (exponential unit) while WGMMA is high‑throughput, and introduces a 2‑stage pipeline where the second GEMM of iteration \(j\) runs while softmax of iteration \(j+1\) runs. However, softmax needs the score matrix \(S^{(j)}\) which is produced by the first GEMM of the same iteration. How is this dependency broken? Is an extra register buffer used to hold \(S^{(j+1)}\) before softmax starts, or does the hardware allow out‑of‑order execution of these instructions?

questions.title: How is block quantization performed for FP8 attention without increasing memory bandwidth?
questions.question_body: The authors claim that block quantization (one scale per tile) can be fused with rotary embedding at no extra cost. I don't understand how the scaling factor is applied to each block: do they quantize \(Q,K,V\) on‑the‑fly during TMA loads, or pre‑scale the tensors in global memory? If scaling is done on‑the‑fly, how is per‑block max/min computed without extra passes over the data?

questions.title: What is incoherent processing and why does multiplying by a random orthogonal matrix reduce FP8 quantization error?
questions.question_body:
In Section 3.3 the paper introduces "incoherent processing" where \(Q\) and \(K\) are multiplied by a random orthogonal matrix \(M\) before FP8 quantization. I would like to know:
1) How does this operation preserve the exact attention output mathematically?
2) Why does spreading out values via \(M\) lead to lower quantization error in practice? Is there any theoretical bound or empirical evidence supporting this claim?

questions.title: How is FLOP counting performed for forward and backward passes in the benchmark section?
questions.question_body:
The authors compute forward FLOPs as
$$4 \cdot \text{seqlen}^2 \cdot \text{head
dim} \cdot \text{num	head
ds}$$
and then halve it for causal masking and multiply by 2.5 for backward pass. Why is there a factor of 4, and why exactly 2.5 for backward? Does this account for recomputation of intermediate softmax values or any extra matrix multiplications?

questions.title: Why does FP8 FlashAttention‑3 underperform for small sequences or causal masking compared to cuDNN?
questions.question_body: In the discussion, authors mention that FP8 FlashAttention‑3 lacks a persistent kernel and load balancing strategy, which hurts performance for short sequences and causal masks. Could someone explain what a persistent kernel is in this context, how it helps with small workloads, and why causal masking exacerbates the issue?
